fields.v: Verner, B. V., Jäckl, B., Rossetto, L., Lokoč, J. (2026). Single-shot Vibe-coded Search Tool For Lifelog Data Layer. In: The 9th Annual ACM Workshop on the Lifelog Search Challenge (LSC '26), June 16-19, 2026, Amsterdam, Netherlands. ACM, pp. 10-17. https://doi.org/10.1145/3810984.3819179
Workshop — LSC '26 (9th Annual ACM Workshop on the Lifelog Search Challenge), Amsterdam, ACM, DOI 10.1145/3810984.3819179
Charles University, Prague, Czech Republic (Verner, Lokoč); Universität Konstanz, Germany (Jäckl); Dublin City University, Ireland (Rossetto)

Evaluates; secondary: Compares — preliminary study of single-shot generation of a lifelog search client (on the PraK data layer and DRES APIs) by three models in GitHub Copilot agent mode with five prompt variants (15 systems), manual feature check, one prompt refinement of the best system, and its use at LSC '26
fields.why: The authors design their own 'single-shot design methodology' (base prompt template plus five prompt variants) and test it; a reader could file the paper as 'Proposes an approach' (then Q13 applies and Q12 may become Partly) rather than 'Evaluates'.
fields.doubt: Os autores criam a 'single-shot design methodology' (prompts próprios) e testam-na. Decide se é Evaluates ou Proposes an approach; se for a segunda, a Q13 aplica-se e a Q12 pode passar a Partly.

fields.v: No SDD approach. GitHub Copilot for VS Code, Agentic Mode (version not stated) with GPT-5.3 Codex (reasoning Xhigh), Claude Opus 4.6 (High) and Gemini 3.1 Pro. Five author-made prompt variants: No Constraints, Paper Information, Useful Features Hinting, Exact Requirement List, Requirements + Planning; plus Exact Requirements + DRES Submission Fix. Base prompt template generated by Gemini 3.1 Pro from the developer's technical specification

One prompt: base template (role and objective, LSC domain and task types, PraK and DRES API specifications with integration rules) plus optional blocks; Exact Requirement List: 8 prioritized requirements; Planning: an 'Architecture & State Design' document (UI layout and component hierarchy, state management) before code

Single shot: prompt → agent generates the complete runnable codebase (Planning variant: architecture document first) → authors test features; for the selected system, prompt refined once and a fresh generation run

None during generation ('without human intervention'); authors manually tested every generated feature afterwards, selected the best system and refined its prompt once (DRES payload format); final tool operated by two participants at LSC '26
Single prompt per system (requirements list and planning document only in two variants); no iterative refinement apart from one prompt update
Not classifiable (authors use 'vibe coding', no SDD terms; the Exact Requirements + Planning variant resembles writing requirements and a design document before code)
New project (client application from scratch on top of the existing PraK data layer API and DRES API)

15 generated systems (3 models × 5 variants), 10 analysed after excluding Gemini, plus 1 refined system; 13 PraK API features, 3 DRES API features and 8 additional features checked; final system a React/TypeScript single-page application (LOC not stated)
Interactive lifelog (multimedia) retrieval client for the Lifelog Search Challenge; React, TypeScript, Zustand
Authors (PraK tool developers and LSC researchers) wrote prompts and tested the systems; final tool used by two competition operators (profile not stated)
None (generation time, tokens and money not reported)
Presence and full functionality of each search feature per generated system, checked manually (Table 1); live competition: operators placed 13th and 16th of 31; tool worked reliably
None measured; qualitative description of the final system's modular architecture (components, services, store; dependency-cruiser graph)
None
Qualitative issues: interface usability (manual ID typing, stale results), functional hallucinations (non-functional UI elements), missing features; 8 additional features added spontaneously

Manual: authors checked each GUI feature (input gathered for the API call and results displayed); dependency-cruiser for the architecture figure; LSC ranking from the live competition. One generation per configuration

Success criterion for all: feature present and fully functional (no overall threshold). (1) GPT-5.3 Codex + GitHub Copilot agent mode (Xhigh), five prompt variants, one run each: text and temporal query worked in all variants; DRES authentication worked, frame and text submission failed; text submission missing in Feature Hinting, Exact Requirements and Exact Reqs + Planning; non-functional elements (Progressive Hints field, Bayes button without candidate selection); per-variant feature counts in Table 1 not reliably recoverable from the extracted text. (2) Claude Opus 4.6 + Copilot agent mode (High), five variants: text and temporal query in all; submission errors; text submission missing in No Constraints; stale results in Exact Reqs + Planning; Exact Requirements system judged best. (3) Claude Opus 4.6 + Copilot, Exact Requirements + DRES Submission Fix (refined prompt, fresh generation): fully functional submission plus earlier search features; used at LSC '26 (operators 13th and 16th of 31, no issues). (4) Gemini 3.1 Pro + Copilot, five variants: interfaces could not display data (unhandled CORS, wrong thumbnail paths); excluded from the analysis. Quality verdict for each: no criterion stated by the authors. Cost verdict: not measured

One task (LSC client for the PraK and DRES APIs). Configurations: 3 models × 5 prompt variants in one agent (Copilot agentic mode), plus one refined prompt. Baseline: none (No Constraints is the least constrained variant). Held constant: agent, base prompt, APIs, maximum reasoning effort; prompts designed without testing generated tools. Acceptance: manual feature check, no automated tests. Repetitions: one generation per configuration. Human intervention: none during generation; one prompt refinement for the final system

No Constraints and Paper Info variants 'highly competitive' in implemented features for both models; more complex prompts did not substantially increase feature success; text and temporal query supported regardless of prompt; upload image query, Bayes update and random frames hard for both models; DRES submission failed in the first 10 systems until the DRES format was specified; additional features sparse (keyboard shortcuts most common). No statistics

Partly: showed feature differences between variants and models (Gemini not testable), but not repeated; authors note repeated runs may give different success rates for one prompt and that Table 1 does not capture usability

Limitations: preliminary study, LLM variance not accounted for, features checked manually, Table 1 ignores usability, base prompt format not validated with the agents; competition problems (thumbnail resolution, no metadata) attributed to the data layer. Gaps / future work: more extensive study with multiple generation trials and automated feature testing

Inconsistencies: 'single-shot' and 'without human intervention' (p. 10) although the final system needed one prompt refinement (stated, p. 14); the model is 'ChatGPT 5.3 Codex' in §5 and 'GPT 5.3 Codex' in Table 1; claim that the tool reduces implementation time 'to an absolute minimum' is not measured (p. 14). Table 1 check marks jumbled in the extracted text, per-variant values not used. Full prompts in the appendix; generated code not released. Authors developed the PraK data layer (Charles University, Konstanz) used as input. Pre-registration: not claimed. Programming language: TypeScript (React)
Yes (1): goal stated (whether recent coding agents can generate a functional LSC client from API specifications)
Partly (0.5): prompts given in full and agent and models named, but the feature-check procedure is informal and the generated systems are not available
Partly (0.5): models and reasoning effort given and GitHub Copilot agent mode named, but no Copilot/VS Code versions or model snapshots
Partly (0.5): task and prompts described; DRES API public (OpenAPI link), PraK API only summarised; generated tools not available
Partly (0.5): features checked manually by the authors against API behaviour; the external LSC ranking concerns only the final tool; no acceptance tests
Partly (0.5): feature checklist used as quality measure, loosely defined; no cost metric
Yes (1): two models (Gemini excluded) and five prompt variants evaluated under the same conditions (same agent, base prompt, APIs, maximum reasoning effort, same feature check)
fields.why: Q7 asks for a baseline or an alternative evaluated under the same conditions; two models and five prompt variants were run in the same agent, with the same base prompt and APIs and the same feature check, which meets it. A missing manual-development baseline does not lower the score.
